en: n. a ceremony held after someone's death, at which the body is buried or cremated; a procession to a burial place
ex: Hundreds of people attended the funeral of the famous singer.
數百人參加了那位知名歌手的葬禮。

en: vt. to make a pain, worry or problem less severe; to take over from someone who has been working for some time; to free someone from a duty; to make something less boring
ex: This medicine will relieve the pain in your back.
這種藥能減輕你的背痛。

en: n. a person who does not eat meat or fish; an animal that eats only plants; a. not containing meat; relating to people who do not eat meat
ex: She became a vegetarian because she loves animals.
她因為愛動物而成為素食者。

en: n. the scientific study of the human mind and how it influences behavior; the way a person thinks and feels; the mental characteristics of a person or group
ex: She is studying psychology at university.
她在大學主修心理學。

en: n. a strong feeling of fear about something that is going to happen; a person or thing that causes fear; vt. to be very afraid of something; a. causing fear
ex: I dread the thought of speaking in public.
我一想到要公開演講就害怕。

en: n. the part of your mind that tells you whether your actions are right or wrong; a feeling of guilt about something you have done
ex: He had a guilty conscience after telling the lie.
他說謊後良心不安。

en: vi. to move slowly from side to side or up and down; vt. to influence someone's opinion; n. the movement from side to side; power or influence over someone
ex: The tall trees swayed in the strong wind.
高大的樹木在強風中搖擺。

en: v. to cut a hard material in order to make a shape or pattern; to cut cooked meat into thin pieces; to create something with difficulty
ex: The artist carved a lion out of a block of wood.
藝術家用一塊木頭雕出了一隻獅子。

en: vt. to remove hair from the face or body with a razor; to cut a very thin piece from something; to pass very close to something; vi. to remove hair with a razor; n. the act of removing hair with a razor; a narrow escape from something
ex: He shaves every morning before going to work.
他每天上班前都會刮鬍子。

en: a. graceful and attractive in appearance or manner; simple and clever; of a high standard
ex: She wore an elegant black dress to the party.
她穿著一件優雅的黑色洋裝去參加派對。

en: n. a person who offers to do something without being paid; a person who joins the army by choice; vi. to offer to do something without being forced or paid; a. done by someone who is not paid
ex: Many students volunteer at the local hospital on weekends.
許多學生在週末到當地醫院當志工。

en: adv. in or to another place; somewhere else
ex: If you can't find it here, look elsewhere.
如果你在這裡找不到，就去別處找。

en: vt. to show something that was hidden; to make something known publicly, especially something wrong; to put someone in a situation where they are not protected
ex: The newspaper exposed the corruption of local officials.
報紙揭發了地方官員的貪腐。

en: n. the mixture of gases that surrounds the Earth; the air in a place; the feeling that a place or situation gives you
ex: The restaurant has a warm and friendly atmosphere.
這家餐廳氣氛溫暖友善。

en: v. to move around continuously; to pass from person to person; to send something to a number of people; to flow through a system
ex: Blood circulates around the body through the veins.
血液透過靜脈在體內循環。

en: n. an action taken to achieve a particular purpose; (plural) steps taken to deal with a problem; a unit used to say how big, long or heavy something is; a certain amount of something; vt. to find the size, length or amount of something
ex: The government introduced new measures to reduce air pollution.
政府推出新措施來減少空氣污染。

en: a. able to make someone do or believe something by giving them good reasons; good at making people agree with you
ex: She gave a persuasive speech that changed many minds.
她發表了一場有說服力的演講，改變了許多人的想法。

en: n. a large meeting of people who share a profession or interest; a traditional way of behaving; an official agreement between countries
ex: Thousands of people attended the annual science convention.
數千人參加了年度科學大會。

en: n. a particular way or path from one place to another; a regular journey made by a bus or ship; the way of achieving something; vt. to send something along a particular path
ex: Which route do you take to get to work?
你上班走哪條路？

en: a. using or relating to computer technology; showing information as numbers; (of a clock or watch) showing the time in numbers
ex: We live in a digital age where everything is online.
我們生活在一個什麼都在網路上的數位時代。

en: vt. to make something more difficult to understand or deal with; to make a problem or illness worse; vi. to become more difficult
ex: Adding more rules will only complicate the situation.
增加更多規定只會讓情況更複雜。

en: n. all the people who live in a particular area; a group of people who share the same interests, religion or background; the public in general
ex: Our community organizes a clean-up day every month.
我們的社區每個月舉辦一次打掃日。

en: n. a strong request that something be done; the amount of a product that people want to buy; the need for something; v. to ask for something firmly
ex: There is a high demand for skilled engineers.
對熟練工程師的需求很高。

en: a. dirty or untidy; difficult to deal with because it involves a lot of problems; (of a situation) complicated and confusing
ex: His room was so messy that he couldn't find his keys.
他的房間亂到找不到鑰匙。

en: n. an amount of money that is given to someone regularly, especially to pay for a particular thing; the amount of something that is allowed; a reduction in price; permission or tolerance
ex: He gets a weekly allowance from his parents.
他每週從父母那裡領零用錢。

en: n. one part of a situation, problem or subject; the way something looks; the direction in which something faces
ex: We need to consider every aspect of the problem.
我們必須考慮這個問題的各個方面。

en: n. a place where people work, such as an office or factory; the activities that take place at work
ex: Safety rules are important in any workplace.
安全規定在任何工作場所都很重要。

en: n. a long, formal dress for women; a long loose piece of clothing worn at night; a long piece of clothing worn at university ceremonies; vt. to dress someone in a long garment
ex: She wore a long evening gown to the ball.
她穿著一件長晚禮服去參加舞會。

en: vt. to close or tie something firmly; to attach one thing to another; to direct your attention to something; vi. to become closed or attached
ex: Please fasten your seat belt before takeoff.
起飛前請繫好安全帶。

en: n. a tiny bright piece of fire that flies up from a fire; a short flash of light made by electricity; a small amount of a quality; vt. to cause something to start; vi. to give off sparks
ex: The fire began with a single spark.
大火是從一個火花開始的。

en: n. a feeling of great pleasure or happiness; something that gives you great pleasure; vt. to give someone great pleasure; vi. to take great pleasure in something
ex: The children screamed with delight when they saw the presents.
孩子們看到禮物時高興地尖叫。

en: n. a particular type of animal or plant that has been developed by breeding; a type or kind of something; v. to keep animals so that they produce young; to cause something to grow or develop; to raise children
ex: This dog breed is known for being friendly and smart.
這個犬種以友善聰明聞名。

en: n. the ability to focus all your attention on something; the amount of a substance in a liquid or in a particular area; a large number of people or things gathered together
ex: The exam requires a lot of concentration.
這場考試需要高度專注。

en: n. an official who represents their country in a foreign country; a person who is good at dealing with people without upsetting them
ex: The diplomat met with the foreign minister to discuss trade.
外交官與外交部長會面討論貿易。

en: n. the process of making something or of being made; the way in which something is arranged; a group of planes, ships or troops arranged in a pattern
ex: The geese flew south in a V formation.
雁群以 V 字隊形向南飛。

en: n. the state of being alone or separate from others; the act of keeping something separate from other things; the state of being cut off from a place or group
ex: Patients with the virus were placed in isolation.
感染病毒的病人被隔離。

en: vt. to say that someone has done something wrong; to charge someone with a crime; vi. to make an accusation against someone
ex: She was accused of stealing money from the company.
她被指控偷了公司的錢。

en: v. to laugh in a silly, uncontrolled way, especially in a nervous way; n. a short, quiet laugh
ex: The girls giggled when the teacher made a funny face.
老師做鬼臉時，女孩們咯咯地笑了。

en: vt. to learn something so well that you can remember it exactly; to remember something carefully
ex: I need to memorize fifty new words by Friday.
我星期五前得背熟五十個新單字。

en: a. at a level between the beginner and the advanced; in a middle position; n. a person who has a level of knowledge or skill between beginner and advanced; a thing in the middle
ex: She is taking an intermediate English course.
她正在上中級英文課。
